subject.title: [Bug]: Agents should not be able to access or modify files outside their own working space.

question: Should OpenClaw make per-agent workspace confinement a default hard boundary, and if so should it cover only filesystem tools or the full tool/exec sandbox boundary?
rationale: Current source and docs make host-wide access an intentional trusted-operator default, so changing it is a security and compatibility boundary rather than a narrow bug fix.

options.title: Define a secure default boundary
options.body: Adopt a maintainer-approved default confinement policy, migration/docs path, and regression coverage across file tools and relevant exec surfaces.

options.title: Keep opt-in confinement documented
options.body: Leave host-wide access as the trusted-operator default and close or retitle this only after explicitly deciding the behavior is intended.

options.title: Track only partial hardening
options.body: Land narrow fixes such as relative traversal containment while keeping broader workspace isolation open in a sandbox/config tracker.

recommendation.title: Define a secure default boundary
recommendation.body: Adopt a maintainer-approved default confinement policy, migration/docs path, and regression coverage across file tools and relevant exec surfaces.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the clearest history on `workspaceOnly` policy, docs, and the current security-default framing.
